title: rapid-alignment-weekend-playbook-for-product-ops
content:
Purpose
---
This is a lightweight, execution-first playbook for a 48–60 hour Rapid Alignment Weekend run by Product Ops to converge company OKRs, finalize the exec update deck, and produce the all‑hands slate and speaker assignments. Focus is on decisions and ship‑ready artifacts, not exhaustive debate.

Outcomes (must ship by Monday 10:30am PT)
- Finalized company OKRs (1 pager + owner roster)
- Exec update deck draft (10 slides + speaker notes)
- All‑hands run-of-show with primary/backup speakers and 2 fallback demos
- Decision log populated (who decided what, rationale, follow‑ups, owners, due dates)

Success criteria (how we know the weekend worked)
- Execs sign off on OKR owners and success metrics (email OK)
- Slides are reviewable and in slide master with placeholders filled
- All‑hands run-of-show has backups for each major segment and a contingency script
- No >5 unresolved cross-team dependencies left without owners

Pre-work (before Friday EOD) -- owners in parens
- Consolidate prior quarter retrospective highlights (Eng SRE, Product analytics) (Sofie)
- Draft OKR candidate list from leadership + top 10 signals (sales + CS + research) (Miguel)
- Baseline metrics and current run‑rate deck page (finance) (Priya)
- Rough speaker list and time budget (Host: Asha)

Weekend schedule (framework)
Friday evening (optional kickoff, 2 hrs)
- 6:00–6:15 — Quick context & rules of engagement (Asha)
- 6:15–7:15 — Lightning updates: topline signal doc review (each contributor 3 min)
- 7:15–8:00 — Mapping session: where candidate OKRs land in priority lattice (small groups)

Saturday (deep alignment and drafting)
- 9:00–9:30 — Quick sync and goal calibration (Asha)
- 9:30–11:30 — OKR breakout #1: Product + Eng — craft objectives and 2–3 candidate key results (chairs: Miguel + Sofie)
- 11:30–12:30 — OKR breakout #2: GTM + CS — alignment on revenue/expansion & adoption KRs (chairs: Priya)
- 12:30–1:30 — Lunch (working)
- 1:30–3:30 — Cross-functional matchmaking: merge breakouts, assign owners, surface dependencies
- 3:30–5:30 — Exec update first draft: slides 1–6 (narrative + metrics)
- 5:30–6:30 — Decision hour: pick top 3 objectives and any must‑defer items (execs)

Sunday (finalization and runbook)
- 9:00–10:30 — Exec slide review: slides 7–10 + speaker notes
- 10:30–12:00 — All‑hands run-of-show: finalize script + rehearsals for top sections
- 12:00–1:00 — Lunch
- 1:00–3:00 — Decision log cleanup, action items, owner handoffs, and comms templates
- 3:00–4:00 — Final signoff window (execs available for 1:1 quick approvals)

Roles & responsibilities (fast reference)
- Facilitator/Host: Asha — running time, escalations, finalizing decisions
- OKR editors: Miguel, Sofie — consolidate wording and measurable KRs
- Metrics owner: Priya — ensures every KR has a baseline + target + signal page
- Slide lead: Liam — merges slide edits, enforces template, exports final deck
- Logistics: Product Ops coordinator (TBD) — Zoom rooms, recording, materials

Decision heuristics (how we choose between competing things)
- Ruler: Impact x Reliability x Speed-to-value. Prioritize items with high impact and high confidence that we can deliver within the quarter.
- Escalation threshold: any KR requiring >3 external teams or >$250k incremental spend requires exec pre-approval.
- Tie-breaker: CEO / Head of Product call (pre-agreed) if execs split 50/50.

Working rules (brevity matters)
- Draft first, argue later. If a statement is actionable, write it down and move on.
- Use the parking-lot doc for long technical debates; assign a follow-up owner.
- Keep edits to slides short bullets — avoid reworking language during review windows.

Templates (shortcuts)
- OKR line: Objective (1 sentence): Why it matters (1 sentence). KR1: metric — baseline -> target -> owner.
- Exec slide template: Slide title; 1–2 bullets of context; chart or metric; 1‑line ask (if any); speaker notes (3 lines).
- Decision log entry: Decision; Date; Participants; Rationale; Owner; Follow-ups (due date).

Communication plan (Monday morning cadence)
- 10:30 AM: Exec sign-off snapshot emailed to staff with link to final OKR doc and slides (Asha + Head of Comms)
- 2:00 PM: All-hands prep email with run-of-show + speaker prep notes (Host + People Ops)
- Owners get Slack DM with action items and due dates (Product Ops coordinator)

Risk register (top 6 things to watch)
1) Key exec unavailable for sign-off — mitigation: two exec-delegate confirmations pre-weekend.
2) Metrics incomplete or noisy — mitigation: highlight as uncertainty in slide and assign metric gate owner.
3) Cross-team dependency without owner — mitigation: escalate during 3:30 Saturday session; default owner = head-of-team on the dependency.
4) Last-minute product demo instability — mitigation: have recorded demo fallback and a second lightweight demo.
5) Scope creep during wordsmithing — mitigation: freeze slide text 60 minutes before sign-off window.
6) Comms misalignment — mitigation: run short comms dry-run Sunday 2pm.

Artifacts to deliver (concrete files)
- OKR 1‑pager (Google Doc) — final (Miguel)
- Exec slide deck (Google Slides) — v0.9 for exec review (Liam)
- All‑hands run-of-show (Google Doc with timestamps) — final (Asha)
- Decision log (Google Sheet) — live (Product Ops coordinator)
- Post-weekend action tracker (Jira board) — create tickets for all follow-ups (Owner: Product Ops)

Post-weekend follow-up (next 7 days)
- Day 1 (Mon): Publish OKRs + exec slide deck; owners confirm first 14-day plan in comments (owners)
- Day 3 (Wed): Quick sync with execs on any unresolved gating items (Facilitator)
- Day 7 (Fri): Close decision log items that are purely comms; create epics for larger cross-team work (Product Ops)

Open questions / notes to self
- Do we need a separate privacy/compliance slide for the all-hands? (ask Security)
- Confirm recording consent language for demos (People Ops legal)
- Who will run the Q&A moderation queue during the all-hands? (proposal: People Ops + one eng moderator)

Quick checklists (for run-of-show owners)
- Speaker confirms slides + 2 practice lines by Sunday 3pm
- Backup demo recorded and accessible by Saturday 6pm
- Slide deck exported as PDF and uploaded to comms folder by Monday 9am

Decision log (example entry)
- Decision: Reduce company objective count from 6 -> 4 for focus
- Date: 2024-09-07
- Participants: CEO, Head of Product, Head of Eng, Head of Sales
- Rationale: Signal consolidation, resource limits, and clearer ownership
- Owner: Head of Product
- Follow-ups: Break into team-level KRs by 2024-09-14

Notes for next run: shorten Saturday breakouts to 90 minutes and add an asynchronous pre-read Q&A doc to reduce time-on-call.

---
If you want, I can convert this into a one-page checklist and produce the comms templates for the Monday email and Slack DM.
